limitations: Fresh interpreters, no warmup; OS caches persist and unrelated user work continues.

Wall includes startup, all reads, inspection, 24 controls, the complete selected backend and result/report/artifact saves. Comparison includes native ICP, Open3D GICP and NDT availability; fixed-rig includes its refinement and holdout evaluation. Parent audits are excluded.
Pipeline timer starts at run_calibration entry; it is a subset of subprocess wall.

Evidence timer wraps the existing candidate plus 24-control call, including its reads, preparation and summaries; prior inspection is outside this subset. No additional evaluation or warmup is performed to obtain the phase timing.
Full result parity normalizes only run ID/timestamps and destination paths.
Scope runtime replaces 8 named modules; other code and writers are shared. Loaded module filenames and all source bytes are checked.
Optimizer time is a subset of the same complete run, without extra calls/warmup.
Decode/import timers are subsets of the same run, without extra reads or imports.
The single pair is limited geometry evidence; quality failures remain failures.
Timings are descriptive ranges, not confidence or portable speedup estimates.

Publication normalizes workspace prefixes in commands/metadata only. Complete canonical result strings and original input/config/output/artifact hashes remain unchanged. Archived code is exact Git bytes; working-byte and committed-byte hashes are separate. Recorded short candidate commit IDs are resolved to their full Git commit; canonical result strings retain the original short run.git_commit.
Workers call the public calibration Python API; CLI dispatch is excluded. Worker measurement JSON writes are included in wall. No timings or outliers are discarded.
